chains.title: Alt allele strengthens a GABPA/Ets site in the TERT promoter; GABP is a known TERTp activator but glioblastoma occupancy at this base is unproven

links.claim: GABPA has its own QBiC-SELEX model that passes the gate and shows the alt allele binds more strongly (effect +4.01, z 68.47; alt site 99.8th percentile), and a shared Ets model also shows alt-more binding (effect +2.121, z 166.19). GABPA is expressed in glioblastoma and GABPA ChIP-seq peaks over this variant exist in other biosamples, but no glioblastoma ChIP is available, so occupancy at this element in the disease context is unproven. Literature supports GABP as a TERT-promoter activator at TERTp mutations generally, not this exact base.
The variant lies in the promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530 with DNase, H3K27ac and H3K4me3 signal, and is annotated as a TERT upstream promoter-region variant.
TERT is the nearest protein-coding gene, with its TSS 0.0 kb away, and VEP annotates the variant as a TERT upstream_gene_variant.

Glioblastoma is the expression context and GABPA is expressed there, but no glioblastoma GABPA ChIP-seq is available; GABPA knockout is common-essential rather than lineage-selective, so the cell-type link is weak and not specific.

The phenotype link is inferential: GABP has been reported to activate mutant TERTp generally, and TERTp mutations are common in glioblastoma, but no cited study tests this exact variant or shows GABPA-dependent TERT activation through this base. TERT is not a selective dependency in glioblastoma lines, and GABPA is common-essential, so the lineage-specific phenotype link remains weak.
